metadata.syllabus_name: Natural Language Processing_Xử lý ngôn ngữ tự nhiên
metadata.description: This course provides students with a foundation in core concepts and methods of Natural Language Processing. The course covers text classification, vector space models, probabilistic methods, sequence models, attention, and transformer-based approaches. Through a research-oriented team project, students learn how to define an NLP problem, review related work, select datasets, build baseline and improved models, evaluate results, analyze errors, and report findings clearly. By the end of the course, students are expected to understand major NLP techniques, apply them to real problems, design and compare experiments, and write technical reports and a short research paper.
metadata.tools:
- Jupyter Notebook / Google Colab
- Python libraries: NumPy, NLTK, scikit-learn, TensorFlow / Keras, PyTorch or equivalent as needed for specialization-aligned models
- Git/GitHub for version control, experiment logs, and teamwork
- Reference manager / citation workflow (e.g., Zotero, Mendeley, or equivalent)
- Cloud/GPU server or Colab runtime as needed for project experiments

clos.clo_details: Explain the end-to-end NLP pipeline, text preprocessing, corpus preparation, tokenization, and core linguistic concepts used in natural language processing.
Apply classical NLP methods including vectorization, Naive Bayes, edit-distance reasoning, HMM/POS tagging, n-gram language modeling, and word embeddings to baseline NLP tasks.
Build and analyze neural sequence models for NLP, including feed-forward networks for text, RNN/LSTM/GRU models, and attention-based sequence learning ideas.
Use transformer-based pretrained language models for classification, sequence labeling, retrieval, question answering, and generation-oriented workflows.
Evaluate NLP systems with suitable metrics, perform error analysis, discuss bias and limitations, and justify research conclusions with evidence and reproducible experiments.

Implement an end-to-end NLP research project including problem formulation, data collection or selection, baseline development, improved modeling, evaluation, report writing, short paper writing, and presentation.
Use AI-assisted development tools responsibly to accelerate experimentation, documentation, teamwork, and reflective learning in NLP projects.

schedule.topic: 1. Course Introduction
1.1 NLTK platform introduction, environment setup, and installation guide
1.2 Tutorial: a small hands-on example with NLTK
2. Supervised ML Pipeline, Sentiment Analysis, and Vocabulary Building
2.1 Tweet preprocessing, feature extraction, logistic regression, and cost function
2.2 Tutorial: sentiment prediction, error analysis, and guided discussion
3. Probability, Conditional Probability, and Bayes' Rule
3.1 Priors, posteriors, likelihood, Naive Bayes, and Laplace smoothing
3.2 Tutorial: Naive Bayes classification, baseline comparison, and error analysis
4. Vector Space Models, W/W-W/D Matrices, and Similarity
4.1 PCA, analogy reasoning, vector transformation, and document search
4.2 Tutorial: similarity computation, vector exploration, and project discussion
5. Autocorrect, Candidate Generation, and Minimum Edit Distance
5.1 Dynamic programming, weighted costs, candidate ranking, and language evidence
5.2 Tutorial: autocorrect walkthrough, evaluation, and failure cases
6. Research Problem Formulation and Proposal Design
6.1 Literature search, related-work matrix, and citation/reproducibility plan
6.2 Review Report 1: proposal and literature review
7. POS Tagging, Sequence Labeling, and Markov Chains
7.1 HMM transitions/emissions, Viterbi decoding, and ambiguity resolution
7.2 Tutorial: POS tagging, decoding practice, and error analysis
8. N-grams, Corpus-Based Language Modeling, and Sequence Probabilities
8.1 Sentence generation, autocomplete, perplexity, and smoothing
8.2 Tutorial: n-gram modeling and language model evaluation
9. Word Embeddings, Dense Representations, and Co-occurrence Intuition
9.1 One-hot vectors, embedding objectives, CBOW/skip-gram, and analogies
9.2 Tutorial: embedding exploration, debiasing, and evaluation
10. Baseline Method Selection, Dataset Splits, and Experimental Protocol
10.1 Metrics, ablation/control variables, and error-analysis plan
10.2 Review Report 2: baseline method and experimental design
11. Neural Networks for Sentiment Analysis, Embedding Input, and Forward Propagation
11.1 Dense layers, activations, loss functions, optimization, and regularization
11.2 Tutorial: neural vs classical models for sentiment analysis
12. Recurrent Neural Networks, Sequence Models, and Hidden States
12.1 Sequence prediction, sequence generation, encoder-decoder, and GRU
12.2 Tutorial: RNN/GRU walkthrough and model behavior discussion
13. Long-Term Dependencies, BPTT, and Gradient Issues
13.1 LSTM architecture, named entity recognition, and sequence-labeling evaluation
13.2 Tutorial: LSTM/NER practice and error analysis
14. Siamese Networks, Semantic Similarity, and Triplet Loss
14.1 One-shot learning, embedding-space training, retrieval, and similarity evaluation
14.2 Tutorial: duplicate-question detection and trade-off discussion
15. Model Improvement Review, Baseline vs Improved Models, and Error Categories
15.1 Comparative evaluation, reproducibility evidence, and reporting strategy
15.2 Review Report 3: advanced-model progress and discussion
16. Neural Machine Translation, Seq2Seq, and Information Bottleneck
16.1 Teacher forcing, attention, queries/keys/values, and generation metrics
16.2 Tutorial: attention-based translation and decoding analysis
17. Transformers, Self-Attention, and Positional Encoding
17.1 Masking, multi-head attention, summarization, and state-of-the-art reasons
17.2 Tutorial: transformer applications and comparison with RNNs
18. Transfer Learning, BERT, T5, and Question Answering
18.1 Pretraining vs fine-tuning, reliability, long-sequence challenges, and efficient transformers
18.2 Tutorial: context-based QA and context-window limitations
19. Progress Test on Core NLP Concepts and Project Status
19.1 Review Report 4, final paper structure, figures/tables, citations, and limitations
19.2 Oral Presentation: final paper draft
20. Oral Presentation: final project review and peer feedback
